Here's my strategy: I believe y will be *extremely* competitive. While it has a good value ($58), my priority at y is tied with other applicants. Therefore, I'm likely to be rejected. My next best option is x ($64), which has a higher value than y. While my priority at x is 2, I think I have a good chance of getting in there, especially since many applicants will be focusing on y. If I don't get x, w is my next best option, and I have the highest priority there. z is my last resort.

Therefore, I will rank x as my top choice, hoping to secure a good value with a reasonable chance of acceptance. This is a calculated risk, prioritizing value over the most popular choice. I believe this will increase my chances of ending up with a good outcome.
